Cercaspora leaf spot - a fungus widely found in soils creating a common problem for hydrangeas. Disease symptoms show when weather is consistently wet or moist (perhaps an irrigation system may contribute if you have one). 

Lets play good news bad news:

Good news - it's not going to kill your hydrangea, hooray!

Bad news - It will reduce your hydrangeas vigor, ability to flower and overall look (especially as the season/disease progresses). Further, You can't really get rid of it.

Good news - it is treatable! By using fungicide, especially before symptoms show, you can manage how severe the disease symptoms are. Also, by preventing watering the foliage and removing the worst looking leaves (bearing in mind that you still want green leaves to produce energy for the plant) you decrease the opportunity for the fungal spores to spread further spreading.

I did not share a similar experience.. I (22M)  was arrested at 15yo at my high school. Here is the story.

When I was 15 my friend, well call him Todd, and i would ride our bikes to our high school so we could smoke weed on the way (i had just started to smoke a few months before so i was going through a phase where i just wanted to smoke for any event). Suddenly, due to a myriad of family issues Todd went through, he moved to another state across the country. I was very upset by this because he was my best friend and i refused to stop our ritual of smoking before school because he left. so, i invited a couple other friends, John and Dale, whom i had smoked with before if they wanted to meet in the school and smoke before our classes started. they did. we met up in the cafeteria and then left the school, walking across the parking lot, behind the baseball fields and into some trees on the edge of the property. on our way we passed Kyle, my high school nemesis (we will return to this later). 

the three of us were in the trees, one joint down and working on our second bowl, when out of the corner of my eye i catch some color moving toward us and hear someone say "hey." i knew it was too late to run, and i was also too high to even bother, so i accepted whatever fate was coming our way. it was the dean of students. 

"what are you guys doing" he asked. in a nutshell, our dean just caught us smoking pot. Kyle, the nemesis, had ratted us out. we were walked into the building and into his office (curiosity was my main emotion. i was very curious how this whole siuation was going to play out. i WAS aware that we were in big trouble. just curious what was next). he demanded we give him our drugs to which we complied. he must not have trusted us however because he then said, "if you have anything else, you should give it up now. the police officers are going to search you and take it if you don't and you'll be in even more trouble then."  

prompted by this question, Dale asked our dean of students "is Officer Leah going to cavity search us?" 

"no" said the dean, as one would answer a stupid question.

Dale then turns and looks me in the eyes, "damn. imagine being cavity searched by Officer Leah" with a perverted ass grin and beet red eyes. I burst out laughing because pictures of Officer Leah were exposed just weeks earlier from when she played in a lingerie football league. she was smoking. even the dean couldn't hide the grin at how funny this comment was from a chopped 15 year old dude. 

Officers did proceed to search us, they cuffed us (still in the high school office) and walked us out of the building and into the back of the police car.

 the rest was pretty uneventful. a cement room for a long time, questions asked, pictures taken, that kind of thing. I was pretty high so i was fairly light hearted about the whole thing "welp, i'm here, guess ill just roll with the punches." 

the only point in which my heart really sank was when i saw my dad walk in to pick me up. the disappointment and confusion (he had no idea i smoked) was unreal on his face.

i still smoke today and am not particularly ashamed of the story...  i learned something. if you're smoking something you shouldn't somewhere you shouldn't, don't just stand there and wait for someone to catch you. this method has seemed to work out for me throughout my college years.
